newsitem.title: LEBANON: Most shares steady in active Beirut trade.
newsitem.headline: Most shares steady in active Beirut trade.

text.p: Most active shares held steady on lower turnover on the Beirut Stock Exchange on Wednesday but brokers said there was an excess of liquidity in the market as investors continued to switch from treasury bills to shares.
The LIBX bank index held steady at 121.17, the BLOM stock index rose 0.31 percent to 908.78 and the LISPI index rose 0.25 percent to 85.76.
Total BSE turnover dropped to 152,578 shares from 226,909. Value was $1,443,613 against $2,469,162 on Tuesday.
However, six of the nine listed shares were traded and brokers said they considered the market active.

"There is remarkable activity. The yields of treasury bills have decreased and those who own matured t-bills and did not want to renew them are investing in the stock exchange now and this has created an excess of liquidity in the market," a broker told Reuters.
"It seems that investors prefer bank shares more than others because they believe they are more profitable," he added.
The two bank shares, Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce and Banque Audi were unchanged in heavy demand at $14.25 and $19.125. Trading in a third bank, Bank of Beirut, is due to start on Friday.
Ciments Libanais rose to $1.25 from $1.21875 on turnover of 11,500 shares compared with 100 a day earlier.
Eternit was unchanged at $2.0312 amid strong demand but turnover fell to 28,460 shares from 41,200.
Solidere A and B were unchanged at $10.25 and $10.75. Turnover fell to 83,205 from 126,383.
There was no trade in the two other listed firms: Ciments Blancs and Uniceramic.
